==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|your}}, {{m|enm|youre}}, {{m|enm|ȝour}}, {{m|enm|ȝoure}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ēower}}, {{m|ang|īower|t=your|pos=plural}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*iuwar}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*izweraz}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|jou|t=your}}, {{cog|nl|jouw|t=your}}, {{cog|nds-de|jo}}, {{m|nds-de|jos|t=your}}, {{cog|de|euer|t=your|pos=plural}}, {{cog|da|jeres|t=your}}.

* {{alt|en|yo|yo'||African American Vernacular}}

====Determiner====
{{head|en|determiner|cat2=possessive determiners}}

# Belonging to you; of you; related to you (singular; one owner).
#: {{ux|en|Let’s meet tomorrow at '''your''' convenience.}}
#: {{ux|en|Is this '''your''' cat?}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Justin Curto|title=The 1975’s Matty Healy Prefers Writing Lyrics He’s Afraid Of|magazine={{w|Vulture.com|Vulture}}|url=https://www.vulture.com/2022/10/the-1975-being-funny-in-a-foreign-language-lyrics.html|date=2022-10-14|passage=Everyone always asks what my advice is, and my advice is don’t overintellectualize '''your''' art.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221018174008/https://www.vulture.com/2022/10/the-1975-being-funny-in-a-foreign-language-lyrics.html}}
# Belonging to you; of you; related to you (plural; more owners).
#* {{RQ:King James Version|John|6|7|column=1|passage=Then Ieſus ſaid vnto them, My time is not yet come: but '''your''' time is alway ready.}}
# A determiner that conveys familiarity and mutual knowledge of the modified noun.
#: {{ux|en|Not '''your''' average Tom, Dick and Harry.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Your''' Show of Shows}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Your''' World with Neil Cavuto}}
#: {{ux|en|Not '''Your''' Average Travel Guide}}
# {{lb|en|Ireland}} That; the specified (usually used with a human referent)
#: {{ux|en|'''Your''' man just bought a new car.}}
#: {{ux|en|Have you seen what '''your''' one over there is doing?}}

Disco, Occasionally. grammatically correct?|date=2026-01-22|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/jan/22/harry-styles-album-kiss-all-the-time-disco-occasionally-grammar|passage=In a possible case of nominative determinism, [Harry] Styles clearly demonstrated his penchant for grammar at a 2015 show, adding an apostrophe and an E to a Philadelphia fan’s sign so it said “You’re so nice” rather than “'''your''' so nice” (he then wrote “thank you – love, Harry” and gave it back, in case there was any doubt about the sign’s message).}}

=====Usage notes=====
* The use of ''your'' instead of {{m|en|you're}} is a common mistake in written English.
